level1_summaries.content: This study developed deep learning models to objectively quantify joint attention behaviors and distinguish autism spectrum disorder (ASD) from typical development (TD) using video data. visual_elements.content: The figure consists of two bar graphs (A and B) illustrating the performance of models for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) detection and symptom severity assessment. Graph A shows the performance of models in distinguishing between ASD and typical development (TD). Graph B presents the performance in differentiating between non-ASD and mild/moderate ASD versus severe ASD. For both graphs, the y-axis represents the 'Estimate, %', indicating the performance metric value. The x-axis shows four different metrics: AUROC (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve), Accuracy, Precision, and Recall.  Each metric has three bars representing different models: IJA (Initiation of Joint Attention), RJA low (low-level Response to Joint Attention), and RJA high (high-level Response to Joint Attention). Error bars indicate the 95% confidence intervals. Generally, for ASD vs TD (A), all three models perform well, close to 100% across all metrics.  For Non-ASD vs mild or moderate ASD vs severe ASD (B), the IJA model tends to have higher values across all metrics compared to the RJA models.

visual_elements.content: The text describes several figures illustrating gaze patterns in individuals with TD and ASD during different tasks. Specifically, it describes a triadic gaze pattern in TD individuals during the IJA task, where they shift gaze between a toy object, the examiner, and back. In contrast, ASD individuals fail to gaze on either the toy or the examiner.  It also describes a heatmap of gaze during a low-level RJA task, where TD individuals maintain gaze on the presented toy object for longer durations, while ASD individuals' gaze remains on the toy object only briefly before wandering. In the high-level RJA task, TD individuals turn to view a poster and then the examiner, while ASD individuals show delayed or no response.
